key_insight: Symbolic regression discovers an interpretable analytical chain for skin friction that generalizes from inviscid surface data to viscous attached flows across subsonic and supersonic regimes.
engineering_relevance: The result enables fast, low-cost skin-friction and drag estimation for airfoils without relying on expensive high-fidelity CFD at every design iteration.
method: Use limited Euler-surface quantities and viscous skin-friction data from airfoils as training input.
Apply symbolic regression to progressively build a formula chain: baseline logarithmic decay, pressure-coefficient correction, then Mach-number correction.
Interpret each added term as a physically meaningful scaling law that links to classical theory when corrections vanish.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on typical geometries with low average integrated skin-friction drag prediction error and good generalization across freestream conditions and shapes.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the attached-flow assumption and on the representativeness of the training data across Mach number and geometry variations.
paper_title: Skin friction prediction for attached flows based on two-dimensional inviscid solutions
